text:
Chao W: heads up — opened a PR that upgrades our gpupool Terraform module from v2.1.0 -> v3.0.0. It’s a breaking change: provider refactor + KMS input shape changes. tagging @anna and @kevin for rollout plan.
Anna L: saw the PR. high level: what breaks in gitops overlays? any state moves required?
Chao W: overlays that pin the module via registry source will get new schema errors. The big ones: `kms_key_id` renamed to `kms_config.id`, and `provider = aws` -> module now expects provider alias per-az. plan shows replacements for `aws_iam_role.gpu_node` (rename) and `aws_subnet_attachment` (recreate due to az-affinity change).
Kevin B: recreate for subnet attachments is scary during scale-up. Do we have a safe migration path? can we avoid replacement for existing pools?
Chao W: proposal in PR body: 1) ship a compat shim in v3 that reads `kms_key_id` and maps it into `kms_config.id` (no state change). 2) add `provider_alias` defaulting to main provider to avoid forcing provider_alias changes. 3) add an automated tfstate migration helper script for customers who opt into a stricter migration.
Maria S: +1 for compat shim. For KMS shape, need to ensure we don't widen permissions. The shim must not accept plaintext ARNs — only cross-account tokenized aliases we already audit.
Alex P: should also add a preflight CI check in the gitops operator that runs `terraform providers` + `terraform plan -target=module.gpupool` against a replica workspace. If plan shows replacements for `aws_subnet` or `aws_iam_role` we block the merge with a clear message.
Chao W: exact. I added a `make preflight` target that runs `TF_IN_AUTOMATION=1 terraform plan -out=tfplan` and a script that parses `resource_changes` for `delete`/`create` pairs. snippet:
```bash
TF_IN_AUTOMATION=1 terraform plan -json > plan.json
jq -r '.resource_changes[] | select(.change.actions | index("create") and index("delete")) | .address' plan.json
```
Anna L: nice. How do we propagate the lockfile? we can’t flip the registry version in 200 overlays at once.
Kevin B: we should push a lockfile change and a repo-level policy that prevents auto-updates, then rollout by teams. Steps: 1) publish v3, 2) publish v3-compat patch with shim, 3) branch protection + repo-level CODEOWNERS update to force manual approvals for module bumps, 4) run a batch job that opens PRs per overlay with bump+preflight output attached.
Chao W: builder job (gitops-bot) already has perms to open PRs. I can add the `preflight` run and attach plan.json to each PR. For overlays that fail preflight we leave them on the v2.x line and tag owners.
Maria S: add KMS acceptance tests to the CI matrix. We should spin up a tiny infra env (no GPUs) but with IAM/KMS mocking using localstack or sts assume-role to validate no permission escalation.
Alex P: also flag cost impact: v3 defaults to per-az provider aliases which may create extra networking attachments in some AZs and trigger ephemeral GPU capacity requests. Add a cost estimate step: check for `aws_subnet_count` diffs and multiply by per-subnet tagging cost bucket, include in PR desc.
deploy-bot: CI / preflight check queued for chao/gpupool-bump (job id: 8811) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Chao W: thanks — running now. will keep a canary pool in us-west-2a pinned to v3-compat for 48h, then escalate.
Anna L: good. please add a rollback playbook in the PR: how to pin back to v2, how to revert TF state if someone accidentally runs apply. make it step-by-step with `terraform state mv` examples.
Chao W: will do. example rollback snippet in PR:
```bash
# move renamed IAM role back to previous address if needed
terraform state mv module.gpupool.aws_iam_role.gpu_node module.gpupool.aws_iam_role.gpu_node_old
```
Kevin B: once preflight passes we still need an operator-level guard: the gitops operator should delay applying module bumps by 30m and re-run plan after 3 reconciles to ensure no drift.
Maria S: logging: add an audit event for any module version change that includes who approved it and the preflight plan output location.
Chao W: agreed. thanks all — will update the PR with shim, preflight job, cost-check, and rollback playbook. ping me if you want to join the canary test tomorrow.
Anna L: thx. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: CI / preflight check completed for job 8811 — plan attached (status: partial-success) :white_check_mark:
Chao W: plan shows 2 overlays flagged (subnet recreate), opening PRs next.
